operations.evidence: The police-use-of-firearms release covers the 43 territorial police forces in England and Wales.
It does not represent every UK police body or every armed security activity.
A police firearms operation is an authorised deployment of armed officers where firearm use may be necessary to protect officers or others.
An authorised deployment does not mean a firearm was fired.
An armed response vehicle is adapted to transport trained armed officers and specialist equipment rapidly to incidents.
An ARV operation count is not a count of vehicles, officers or shots.
The release counts incidents in which police firearms were discharged at persons.
Incident counts are not the number of firearms fired or shots discharged.
Armed-officer statistics are a snapshot as at 31 March 2026.
A snapshot does not measure staffing throughout the whole year.
Separate police-use-of-force statistics include wider firearm tactics and are not directly comparable because definitions and collection differ.
Figures from the two series must not be merged without harmonisation.
There were 17,584 police firearms operations in the year ending 31 March 2026.
The national total does not establish local danger or parcel-level risk.
Ninety-three percent of firearms operations in the year ending March 2026 involved an ARV.
The ARV share is a subcategory proportion, not a measure of firearm discharge.
There were nine incidents in which police discharged firearms at persons in the year ending March 2026.
Small annual counts are volatile and should not be converted into precise local probabilities.
Operationally deployable armed officers exclude officers absent through sickness or on restricted duties.
Total armed officers and deployable armed officers are different measures.
Operations where officers were stood down before deployment are excluded from firearms-operation totals.
Excluded stand-downs must not be inferred from published totals.
VIP protection, armed prisoner escorts, airport patrols, guarding duties and routine patrols are excluded from firearms-operation totals.
The statistics do not measure all armed-officer activity.
Accidental discharges, animal destruction, police training and tyre deflations are excluded from the operation discharge measure.
Excluded discharge types must not be added to incidents fired at persons.
Operations involving ARVs are a subcategory where the first or only response was by an ARV.
All firearms operations include the ARV subcategory, so the figures must not be added together.
A discharge incident count does not equal the number of weapons fired or shots fired.
Shot volume cannot be derived from incident totals.
Discharge-at-person figures exclude less-lethal weapons such as attenuating energy projectiles and conducted energy devices.
The series is not a complete measure of all force tactics.
City of London is excluded from per-100,000 force comparisons because its population estimate is below 100,000.
Rate tables do not provide a complete comparison for every force area.
The latest release incorporates revisions to previous-year figures submitted by forces.
Historical values must be versioned because later releases can supersede them.
Some forces interpreted operationally deployable differently during COVID-19 and could not fully comply with the required definition because of system restrictions.
Pre-2022 deployability comparisons may contain small inconsistencies.
The data are mandatory Annual Data Requirement returns and undergo variance, completeness, duplicate and validity checks with all forces.
Mandatory collection and QA do not make the data suitable for exact-address inference.
